input.quote: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: The cap in 21.1 is mutual, but its basis is only one month of Fees actually paid — far below the fallback of 12 months' fees and inside walk-away territory (a cap below six months' fees). The words "without exception" also override the Excluded Claims regime in 21.3, placing indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap, which the playbook treats as walk-away. Sections 21.2 (mutual exclusion of indirect damages, with restoration/replacement costs preserved as direct) and 21.3 (Excluded Claims definition; Customer's payment obligation is not damages) are otherwise at the preferred position, so the minimal fix is to correct 21.1's cap basis and reinstate the carve-out.

ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, which are not subject to this limitation, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, as a one-month fee cap is not a meaningful remedy for either Party. We have also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) sit outside the cap, as Section 21.3 already contemplates.
proposal.summary: Raise the mutual liability cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and carve out Excluded Claims.
